**An open-source UI component library for building high-quality, accessible design systems and web apps.**

Radix Primitives is a low-level UI component library with a focus on accessibility, customization and developer experience. You can use these components either as the base layer of your design system, or adopt them incrementally.

excerpts.text:
export const Styled = () => (
  <AlertDialog.Root>
    <AlertDialog.Trigger className={styles.trigger}>delete everything</AlertDialog.Trigger>
    <AlertDialog.Portal>
      <AlertDialog.Overlay className={styles.overlay} />
      <AlertDialog.Content className={styles.content}>
        <AlertDialog.Title className={styles.title}>Are you sure?</AlertDialog.Title>
        <AlertDialog.Description className={styles.description}>
          This will do a very dangerous thing. Thar be dragons!
        </AlertDialog.Description>
        <AlertDialog.Action className={styles.action}>yolo, do it</AlertDialog.Action>
        <AlertDialog.Cancel className={styles.cancel}>maybe not</AlertDialog.Cancel>
      </AlertDialog.Content>
    </AlertDialog.Portal>
  </AlertDialog.Root>
);

synthesis.guidance: Use the Root/Portal/Overlay/Content hierarchy from the inspected alert-dialog story, preserving Title and Description rather than styling an anonymous floating card. Size the dialog from the real decision text and place a clearly named cancel action beside the consequential action. Replace the upstream joke labels with actual consequences; do not copy its financial scenario or external imagery. Choose alertdialog only for an interruption requiring a decision, not every informational overlay. Keep existing brand typography and quiet surfaces: the primitive supplies behavior, not a finished visual identity. Test Tab, Escape, initial focus and focus return with the installed version. The excerpt is not a runnable bundle; upstream CSS is omitted.

synthesis.summary: A compound alert-dialog composition separates trigger, overlay, accessible title, description, confirm action and cancel action. Useful for consequential changes in settings or account screens.
